rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the priority is to establish a clean, minimal baseline. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest configuration in the space: it uses basic PCA for dimensionality reduction, a single profile, and no aggregation or fusion. This gives a clear reference accuracy for the RNA modality alone, which is essential for later determining whether (a) image data adds signal, (b) more complex RNA encoders (scVI, scGPT) improve over PCA, (c) multiprofile + aggregation helps, and (d) multimodal fusion provides a gain over the best single modality. Starting from the simplest setup reduces confounds and lets each subsequent experiment isolate one design choice. It is the most information-dense first step under a tight 10-experiment budget.

With only one completed experiment (config_001: rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000 → 48.5% acc), the largest source of uncertainty is whether the image modality carries useful signal at all. config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the simplest image baseline and directly tests this question in isolation. If image accuracy is competitive or better than the RNA baseline, it strongly motivates investing remaining budget in multimodal configurations; if it is substantially worse, we can deprioritize image and multimodal configs and focus on RNA encoder and profile improvements. This single experiment bifurcates the search space and is the highest-information next step before committing to more complex multimodal or multiprofile designs.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieves 0.485 accuracy while image (ResNet50) is weak at 0.208, establishing RNA as the dominant modality. The key uncertainty is whether a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) can substantially outperform the simple linear PCA reduction. This experiment (config_004) directly compares scvi_n200 vs PCA n2000 while holding profile setting (single) and model setting (rna_only) constant, cleanly isolating the effect of the RNA representation. If scvi_n200 improves accuracy, it justifies investing further experiments in learned encoders and multimodal fusion with that encoder; if not, PCA is sufficient and we should pivot to testing aggregation (multiprofile) or better image encoders. With 7 experiments remaining, this single-variable comparison is the highest-information next step before committing budget to more complex multimodal configurations.

Evidence: scvi_n200 (config_004, 0.5203 acc) outperforms pca_n2000 (config_001, 0.4849 acc) as an RNA encoder, and image-only (config_010, 0.2079 acc) is very weak, suggesting RNA modality drives performance. Uncertainty: it is unknown whether multiprofile aggregation adds value on top of the best singleprofile encoder. This experiment (config_005: rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) is a clean one-variable extension of the current best (config_004), isolating the effect of multiprofile + avgpool aggregation while holding the encoder constant. It is the best use of this slot because the multiprofile/aggregation question is structurally central—it determines whether 20+ downstream multiprofile and multimodal configurations are worth pursuing, and answering it early with a simple aggregation (avgpool) before trying transformer keeps the comparison interpretable and conserves budget for later exploitation.

The strongest result so far is config_005 (RNA-only, multiprofile, scVI_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 acc, showing that multiprofile + avgpool is a major boost over single-profile. The key open question is whether transformer aggregation can further improve over avgpool for the same encoder/profile setting. config_006 isolates exactly this variable (transformer vs avgpool) while holding RNA encoder (scVI_n200) and profile setting (multiprofile) constant. This is the highest-value next experiment because: (1) it directly exploits the best-performing direction, (2) it cleanly separates the aggregation effect so we know whether to invest remaining budget in transformer-based multimodal configs (config_032/033/038/039) or stick with avgpool, and (3) with only 5 experiments left, resolving this design choice early prevents wasting budget on a suboptimal aggregation strategy across all subsequent multimodal trials.

Evidence: The current best (config_006, rna_only/multiprofile/scvi_n200/transformer, acc=0.653) shows that multiprofile with scvi_n200 is the dominant direction, and transformer vs avgpool aggregation makes negligible difference (~0.003). The image-only signal is very weak (0.208), making multimodal fusion less immediately promising. Uncertainty: We have not yet tested whether scgpt, a more specialized and recent RNA foundation model, outperforms scvi_n200 as an encoder. This experiment isolates the encoder variable (scgpt vs scvi_n200) while holding profile=multiprofile and aggregation=transformer at their best-known settings. It is the best use of this slot because it is a clean single-variable comparison that could establish a stronger RNA baseline before investing remaining budget in more complex multimodal or aggregation choices. If scgpt substantially improves accuracy, it reshapes the optimization landscape for the final 4 experiments; if not, we confirm scvi_n200 as the best encoder and can pivot to testing multimodal fusion or other refinements.

Evidence: RNA-only multiprofile with scvi_n200 and transformer aggregation is the clear best (0.6530), far exceeding image-only (0.208) and other RNA encoders. The critical open question is whether fusing the weak image signal with the strong RNA multiprofile representation can push accuracy above 0.65, or whether the weak image features will dilute the RNA signal. This experiment (config_032: multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) is the most direct logical extension of our best result, changing only the model setting from rna_only to multimodal with concat fusion. It isolates the effect of adding the image modality to the proven-best RNA pipeline. If it improves over 0.6530, the remaining 3 experiments can explore fusion strategy (weighted) and image encoder (ViT-L); if it does not, we confirm RNA-only is optimal and can focus remaining budget on marginal refinements. This is the highest-information experiment given the 3-experiment remaining budget.

The current best is config_032 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, concat) at 0.688 acc. The only untested variation of this exact architecture is the fusion method: config_033 swaps concat for weighted fusion, isolating a single variable. This is a clean A/B test that directly exploits the strongest evidence in the search. If weighted fusion improves accuracy, we gain a refinement on the best configuration; if not, we confirm concat is optimal and can dedicate the final experiment to testing a stronger image encoder (ViT-L, config_038). Given only 2 experiments remain, this low-risk, high-information comparison is the best use of experiment 8 to either lock in an improvement or confirm the current architecture before the last exploration.

The current best is config_033 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + multiprofile + transformer + weighted) at 0.7131. The image-only resnet50 was very weak (0.208), yet adding it to the multimodal pipeline still yielded a ~6% boost over RNA-only multiprofile (0.653). This suggests the image encoder is underperforming and a stronger backbone could unlock more signal. Config_039 isolates exactly one change from the best configuration: replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l while keeping scvi_n200, multiprofile, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion fixed. This directly tests whether a more powerful image representation improves fusion quality. With only 1 experiment remaining after this, testing the highest-leverage unexplored variable (image encoder) on the proven best pipeline is the most efficient use of the budget to either find a new best or confirm the ceiling.

The current best is config_039 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 accuracy. Evidence strongly supports scvi_n200 as the best RNA encoder, multiprofile as essential, weighted fusion over concat (0.7131 vs 0.6878 with resnet50), and imagenet_vit_l over resnet50 (0.7250 vs 0.7131). The one remaining untested variable in this best-performing family is aggregation: transformer vs avgpool. In RNA-only multiprofile, the difference was negligible (0.6530 vs 0.6501), but in the multimodal setting with a stronger image encoder, the interaction could shift. Config_037 (avgpool + weighted + imagenet_vit_l) isolates this single change from the current best. As the final experiment, this is the most informative test: if it matches or beats config_039, it reveals aggregation is not a bottleneck; if it falls short, it confirms transformer is the right choice and solidifies config_039 as the definitive best. No other untested configuration has a realistic chance of exceeding 0.7250 given the strong evidence against scgpt, pca_n2000, or concat fusion.
